Definition: apparently a primary word; a spot (generally in space, but limited by occupancy; whereas G5561 is a large but particular locality), i.e. location (as a position, home, tract, etc.); figuratively, condition, opportunity; specially, a scabbard:--coast, licence, place, X plain, quarter, + rock, room, where.
BiblicalUsage: Place is the plainest word in the New Testament, and Paul uses it to say where the church is. The church of God at Corinth is joined with all that in every place call upon the name of Jesus Christ, and from Thessalonica the word of the Lord sounded out into every place.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word's plainness is its power: every place means every place, and the gospel is not bound to one city.
